examples.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Chain Rule
examples.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $\textrm{arccot}$ is

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}(\textrm {arccot } x) 	=  -\dfrac 1 {1+x^2}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\,\text{arccot }({x}^{2}+5)) \\  & =2\cdot (-\frac{1}{1+({x}^{2}+5)^{2}})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+5) \\  & =-\frac{2}{1+({x}^{2}+5)^{2}}\cdot 2x \\  & =-\frac{4x}{1+({x}^{2}+5)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{4x}{{x}^{4}+10{x}^{2}+26}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve $f(x)=-7arccscx$ at $x=\sqrt{5}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arccsc$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7arccscx) \\  & =-7\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}) \\  & =\frac{7}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{5}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{5}) & =\frac{7}{|\sqrt{5}|\sqrt{{\sqrt{5}}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5-1}} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$
